dimensions.assessment: Applies to the Department of State, USAID, federal contractors, and program partners operating abroad.
dimensions.evidence: No funds authorized to be appropriated to the Department of State or the United States Agency for International Development may be used

dimensions.assessment: Bans the use of funds for programs utilizing goods tied to forced labor in Xinjiang unless strict waiver assurances and congressional notices are met.
dimensions.evidence: knowingly uses goods... mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region

dimensions.assessment: Restricts the use of existing authorized appropriations for the Department of State and USAID without altering total federal spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: No funds authorized to be appropriated to the Department of State or the United States Agency for International Development may be used

dimensions.assessment: Places explicit statutory restrictions on federal foreign affairs spending, contracting compliance, and annual reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State shall submit... a report on an annual basis for three years

dimensions.assessment: Permanent restrictions on fund usage, accompanied by a three-year mandatory reporting requirement.
dimensions.evidence: submit to the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House... a report on an annual basis for three years

missing_information: The monetary value of contracts or programs affected by the restriction is not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill prohibits the Department of State and USAID from using appropriated funds on policies, programs, or contracts that knowingly use goods from Xinjiang or associated forced labor entities, subject to specific waiver and reporting rules.
